"Celebrity Octagon Clash es un videojuego de artes marciales mixtas (MMA) en 3D que traslada la intensidad, brutalidad y espectáculo de la UFC al universo de la cultura popular global. En lugar de luchadores profesionales tradicionales, el Roster principal está formado por deportistas de élite, influencers, actores, músicos y empresarios de la vida real.
El juego combina la profundidad técnica del sim-fighting (control de distancia, striking técnico, grappling, gestión de stamina) con el tono satírico y espectacular de los eventos Pay-Per-View mediáticos.El juego cuenta con personajes modelados hiperrealistamente en 3D (estilo Unreal Engine 5), con animaciones capturadas y voces reales o imitaciones autorizadas:
Tech @COMMENT_BODY@ Business: Elon Musk (Estilo: Kickboxing experimental, gadgets visuales), Mark Zuckerberg (Estilo: Jiu-Jitsu Brasileño técnico, alta resistencia).
Influencers @COMMENT_BODY@ Content Creators: Logan Paul, Jake Paul, Ibai Llanos, KSI, ElRubius (Estilos adaptados a sus disciplinas reales y atributos físicos exagerados).
Hollywood @COMMENT_BODY@ Cine: Dwayne \"The Rock\" Johnson (Grappler pesado), Jason Statham (Striker rápido), Tom Cruise (Especialista en parkour y takedowns impredecibles).
Música @COMMENT_BODY@ Cultura Pop: Snoop Dogg (Counter-striker evasivo), 50 Cent (Brawler de impacto directo), Bad Bunny (Luchador aéreo/showman).Mecánicas Principales de Gameplay
A. Sistema de Striking (De Pie)
Deformación facial en tiempo real: Cadenas de impacto que causan cortes, hinchazón y sangre procesada por simulación de fluidos.
Gestión de Estamina y Daño Lcalizado: El daño acumulado en las piernas reduce la movilidad; los golpes continuos a la cabeza aumentan la probabilidad de Flash KO.
Momentum del Público: Cuanto más arriesgada o espectacular sea la combinación, más sube la barra de \"Hype\", otorgando un ligero aumento en velocidad de reacción y fuerza.
B. Sistema de Grappling y Suelo (Takedowns @COMMENT_BODY@ Submissions)
Mini-juego de Sumisión Dinámico: Basado en zonas de presión analógicas donde el atacante intenta cerrar la llave (Armbar, Rear-Naked Choke) y el defensor busca el espacio de escape.
Transiciones en Ground @COMMENT_BODY@ Pound: Posicionamiento táctico (Guardia completa, Montada, Control lateral) con mecánicas de bloqueo y codos cortos devastadores.
C. Habilidades Especiales \"Siganture Move\"
Sin romper el tono de realismo físico del deporte, cada personaje posee un movimiento insignia representativo de su persona pública cuando la barra de Showmanship se llena al máximo (por ejemplo, celebraciones virales, golpes característicos o provocaciones al rival que bajan la moral del oponente).
4. Modos de Juego
Modo Carrera: \"Del Podcast al Cinturón\"
Crea tu propio personaje desde cero o toma a una celebridad de nivel bajo.
Gestiona entrenamientos, campamentos de pelea, promociones en redes sociales, ruedas de prensa agresivas y contratos patrocinados.
Mantén la disciplina para no pasarte del peso antes de la ceremonia del pesaje.
Modo Megafight (Local y Multijugador Online)
Combates rápidos online estructurados en divisiones de peso ficticias (Peso Influencer, Peso Pesado de Hollywood, etc.).
Salas de eventos en directo donde la comunidad puede apostar moneda del juego sobre los resultados de las peleas.
Promoter Mode (Gestión de Eventos)
Conviértete en el \"Dana White\" del circuito. Organiza carteleras, pacta las provocaciones (trash talk) pre-pelea para maximizar el PPV, paga las bolsas de los luchadores y evita que las peleas estelares se cancelen por lesiones de última hora.
5. Estilo Visual, Audio y Presentación
Comentaristas Ficticios/Reales: Entradas triunfales de octágono con luces estroboscópicas, música personalizada para cada personaje y comentaristas de renombre que analizan la trayectoria real y la \"carrera en el ring\" del personaje.
Física Ragdoll Mejorada: Las caídas por KO respetan la inercia del impacto final, creando momentos memorables y repetibles al instante en cámara lenta desde múltiples ángulos. (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Good. Let's scaffold Vite + three. But static start script will run npm ci/install and vite build. Need package.json + package-lock.

Design decision: make a rich game. Let's architect:

Files:
- index.html
- src/main.js — bootstrap, screen management
- src/styles.css
- src/data/roster.js — fighters with stats, colors, signature moves, quotes
- src/engine/arena.js — Three.js scene: octagon, cage, arena bowl, crowd, lights, jumbotron, camera rigs
- src/engine/fighter.js — procedural 3D fighter model with joint hierarchy, facial features, damage/bruise material, animation state machine (idle, stance bob, jab, cross, hook, uppercut, body kick, head kick, takedown, block, dodge, hurt, KO ragdoll)
- src/engine/match.js — combat simulation, AI, hit detection, stamina, damage, hype, showmanship, grappling state machine, submission minigame, commentary
- src/ui.js — HUD, menus, mobile controls, touch joystick, etc.
- src/audio.js — WebAudio synth sound effects & crowd.
- src/game.js — mode flows: main menu, roster select, fight setup, career, promoter.

Gameplay model: Rather than full physics, use a distance-based fighting system with fighters locked facing each other in a 3D ring; player moves around octagon with joystick (x/z), opponent AI moves. Attacks have range/arc checks. Camera follows player, over-the-shoulder-ish, framing both fighters. On mobile: left virtual joystick movement, right buttons: Jab, Power (hook/kick), Grapple, Block, Signature. Plus dodge swipe? Keep buttons: STRIKE, KICK, GRAPPLE, BLOCK, SPECIAL.

Controls keyboard: WASD move, J punch, K kick, L grapple/takedown, Space block, E special. Shift sprint? maybe.

Combat:
- health 100 overall + head/body/legs damage counters. Localized damage affects speed (legs), flash KO chance (head), stamina regen (body).
- Stamina 100 drains per attack, regen; block drains.
- Hype 0-100 gained from combos, risky moves, taunts, crowd; boosts speed/damage.
- Showmanship 0-100, fills with hype, signature move at 100.
- Strike types: jab (fast, low dmg), cross (medium), hook, uppercut, body kick, head kick (high dmg, slow), flying knee (special). Simplification: two attack buttons, tap vs hold? Let's make: Strike button (jab/cross combo chains based on timing), Kick button (leg kick / body kick / head kick chain), Grapple (takedown attempt when close; ground transitions & submission), Block (hold), Special (signature).
- Block reduces damage, drains stamina, guard break.
- Dodge: double tap joystick direction? Or "swipe" on right? Add a dodge button maybe 5 buttons fits. Actually mobile: left stick, right 2x2 grid + special: Strike, Kick / Grapple, Block, plus big SPECIAL. That's 5.
- Grapple minigame: when takedown succeeds, go to ground. Ground UI: pressure zones mini-game: a rotating needle in a bar; tap in green zone to advance position (mount, side control, back), defender AI resists. Submission: bar with moving zone, tap when in target, 3 successes = finish. Opponent can reverse if you miss. Keep it arcade.
- KO: ragdoll tumble with velocity, slowmo, replay from different angles. Announce winner, stats.

Camera: dynamic: default behind player at 4.2m height 2.2 looking at midpoint; when action, slight shake on hits. On KO, orbit cinematic.

Arena: octagon platform (cylinder 8 sides), fence posts + chain-link using transparent texture generated on canvas, canvas mat with logo, crowd ring of low-poly spectators with random colors, jumbotron screens with live "CELEBRITY OCTAGON CLASH" texture, spotlights, haze (fog), arena truss. Should look good with emissive lights and bloom? Post-processing (UnrealBloomPass) might be heavy on SwiftShader. Could use renderer with toneMapping ACES and fake glow sprites. For mobile performance, keep poly counts modest. Maybe optional bloom off. Use 60fps cap.

Fighters: build humanoid with Group hierarchy:
root -> hips -> torso -> chest -> neck -> head, arms upper/lower/hand, legs thigh/shin/foot. Use CapsuleGeometry and SphereGeometry, skin tone materials, distinct shorts, gloves, hair/beard, face features (nose, ears, eyes, eyebrows, mouth), plus tattoo decals maybe simple. Scale ~1.85m tall. Real celebrities likeness is sensitive but we can do stylized caricature; that's fine (satire). Names like "The Rock" etc. It's requested.

Animations procedural: define pose functions by state and time; set rotations on joints. Implement smooth interpolation. States: idle, guard, jab, cross, hook, uppercut, kickLow, kickBody, kickHead, block, hurt, takedown, sprawl, groundTop, groundBottom, submission, victory, KO.

To keep manageable, fighter class with `pose` target and lerp. Use hand/foot world positions for hit sparks.

Hit effects: particle bursts (blood/sweat) using instanced points; screen flash; face bruising via material color lerp and cuts as small red planes appear; head deformations - scale head mesh on hit briefly (facial deformation approximation). Camera shake.

Commentary: text feed with lines from a set, triggered by events, plus two commentators names ("Vinnie 'The Mic' Cruz", "Roxy 'Bones' Delgado"). Speech synthesis? Maybe use SpeechSynthesis for announcer intros - could be fun but unreliable; keep optional toggle off. Use WebAudio crowd noise (filtered noise), impact thuds, bell. That's good.

Modes:
1. Quick Fight (Megafight): select your fighter from roster grid (12 celebs), select opponent (or random), select weight class/venue maybe. Fight.
2. Career: create character (name + style + look), start at ranking 12; train (mini choices), promote (social), fight bouts; win to gain fans/money; weight cut risk; save to localStorage. Career hub UI with stats bars, next fight, training camp, social posts, weigh-in. Each fight uses engine. Progress ranking to title. Simple but functional.

content.text: Created file successfully: src/data/roster.js

Now the audio engine. WebAudio synth: crowd ambience (filtered noise loop), impacts, whoosh, bell, cheer, boo, heartbeat, UI clicks, announcer maybe.

Implement lazy init on user gesture. Master gain, mute toggle. Crowd: create buffer noise 2s looped through lowpass + gain modulated. Cheer bursts via noise + bandpass sweep. Bell via FM sine.

Let's write.
Created file successfully: src/core/audio.js

Now the Three.js fighter. This is the crux visually. Let's carefully design.

Build a group with joints. Use unit humanoid with heightScale.

Body parts:
- root group
- hips group at y ~ 0.98 (hip height). Body height 1.8.
- torso mesh: tapered box or capsule from hips up. Use CylinderGeometry(top r .23, bottom .18, h .5) scaled x1.3 z0.8 -> chest. Add pectoral spheres, abs.
- shorts: cylinder around hips.
- neck cylinder, head group.
- Head: sphere scaled (0.105, 0.135, 0.115) plus jaw box; nose; ears; eyes white spheres + iris; eyebrows; mouth; hair mesh; beard overlay. Head group positioned at neck top. Face forward +Z? Fighters face each other. In Three.js, if we rotate root to face opponent, local forward should be +Z. Build face features at +Z.
- Arms: shoulder groups at chest sides, upper arm cylinder/capsule length .29, elbow group, forearm length .26, glove sphere at end. Local arm down: capsule geometry along Y with center at -len/2. Joint groups at top.
- Legs: hip joints at ±0.11, thigh capsule down .42, knee group, shin .42, foot box forward +Z.
- gloves: sphere radius .085 scaled (1,1.15,1.15), plus wrist band.

Stance: root rotated to face opponent, body angled ~25° in guard. Pose library modifies joints.

Since fighters face +Z locally. Match sets root.rotation.y = atan2(dx, dz) to face target (for +Z forward). Player camera behind player, looking at opponent; player faces away from camera.

Materials per fighter instance: clone skin material for damage tint (bruise). Head material unique; body skin unique too (sweat). Shorts with trim stripes: use canvas texture for shorts? Simple: shorts base + side stripe mesh planes. Add name text on back via CanvasTexture plane? Nice touch: name on shorts back maybe skip.

Hair styles:
- short: sphere cap slightly larger, clipped? Use sphere with thetaLength ~1.6, rotated, plus top. Could use SphereGeometry(r, 16, 12, 0, Math.PI*2, 0, Math.PI*0.55) scaled.
- buzz: thin cap.
- bald: none.
- quiff: cap + box swept.
- fluffy: cap + several spheres.
- braids: cap + long thin capsules hanging back (8).
- goatee/beard: mesh shapes.

Tattoos: use canvas texture on upper arm/chest with simple tribal marks; simpler: dark ring meshes on arm. For shoulder tattoo: a couple of dark curved shapes (TorusGeometry partial) on shoulder.

Glasses for none. Keep.

Add body sweat/gloss via roughness 0.45, env? Without environment map, standard materials look flat. Add a simple RoomEnvironment? three has RoomEnvironment in examples, could import. Or generate PMREM from a simple gradient scene. Use `RoomEnvironment` from three/addons/environments/RoomEnvironment.js — gives nice reflections. Then scene.environment = pmrem. Cost one-time. Good. With ACES tone mapping.

Add contact shadow blob: circle mesh with radial gradient canvas texture, transparent, under fighter.

Ragdoll: fighter has `ko` physics with velocity, angular velocity; limbs limp (set pose weights to zero / lerp to limp). Update root pos and rotation. Add bounce.

Animation poses:

Define joint names: hips, chest, neck, head, shL, elL, shR, elR, hipL, knL, hipR, knR, footL, footR.

All rotations Euler; set via lerp helper. Base guard:
- hips rotation y maybe 0.2 (bladed)
- chest y -0.15
- shL: x=-0.7, y=0.25, z=0.55 (arm raised in front)
- elL: x=-1.4? Since forearm local down, bending elbow forward = x rotation negative? Need think.

Local arm: upper arm geometry extends -Y from shoulder. Rotating shoulder x by -90° swings arm forward (+Z). Elbow rotation x by -90° bends forearm forward relative to upper arm. In guard, arms hang slightly forward: shoulder x=-0.5 (arm forward-down), elbow x=-1.7 (forearm folded up toward chest) — since forearm down from elbow; rotating x negative swings forearm forward/up? If upper arm rotated -0.5 about X, its local -Y points forward-down. Elbow rotation -1.5 more would swing forearm forward-up. Gloves end near chest height. Let's approximate and check screenshot.

Facing: +Z. Camera behind player at -Z looking +Z. Player fighter back to camera. Arms in guard visible.

Punch jab: left shoulder x=-1.55 (arm horizontal forward), z maybe +0.15; elbow x=-0.15 (extended), hips/chest rotate y. Since arm extends along -Y rotated -90° -> +Z. Good. Hook: shoulder x=-1.4, y rotation to swing across, elbow x=-1.0. Uppercut: shoulder x=-1.1, elbow x=-2.0 (folded), then extend upward.

Kick: hip joint x=-1.5 (leg forward), knee bend. Roundhouse: hip x=-1.3, z rotation and root y rotation.

Poses via library functions with `t` progress. Use keyframe interpolation: define pose at phases [0, windup, impact, recover] and interpolate each joint using easing. That's robust. Implement `poseLib[state] = [{t:0, pose:{...}}, ...]`. Poses only include joints they modify, base guard fills rest. For simplicity define full pose objects for keyframes using helper.

Attack timing & hit frames in match must match animation: define `ATTACKS` table with duration, impactAt, range, arc, damage, cost, type.

Let's define fighter animation API:
- `setAnim(name, opts)` with time reset if name changes.
- `update(dt)`: advance animTime; compute pose blend; apply. Add walk offset when moving.
- `hitReact(headOrBody)`: quick flinch overlay for 0.25s (store flinchT) applied additively to head/chest.
- `setDamage({cuts, bruise})`: update skin tint and blood decals. Blood: small red planes on face/body appear with cuts count; also blood particles from match.
- `setBlocking(bool)`.
- `victory()` raises arms.
- `ko()` ragdoll.

Maybe simpler: use a global "animPose" function returning joint rotations based on state + t. Then fighter.update computes current targets and lerps with rate.

Let's write.

For face: create eyes (white spheres with dark iris), brows (boxes), nose (cone), mouth (thin box), ears. Add lips. To show "hyperrealistic" stylization, use skin material with slight subsurface fake (MeshPhysicalMaterial with sheen? expensive). Use MeshStandardMaterial with roughness .5.

Fighter size: heightScale multiplies root.scale uniformly? Use root.scale.setScalar(heightScale) but positions in match ground; fine. Build scale via look.heightScale.

Let's code fighter.js.
Created file successfully: src/three/fighter.js

"Celebrity Octagon Clash es un videojuego de artes marciales mixtas (MMA) en 3D que traslada la intensidad, brutalidad y espectáculo de la UFC al universo de la cultura popular global. En lugar de luchadores profesionales tradicionales, el Roster principal está formado por deportistas de élite, influencers, actores, músicos y empresarios de la vida real.
El juego combina la profundidad técnica del sim-fighting (control de distancia, striking técnico, grappling, gestión de stamina) con el tono satírico y espectacular de los eventos Pay-Per-View mediáticos.El juego cuenta con personajes modelados hiperrealistamente en 3D (estilo Unreal Engine 5), con animaciones capturadas y voces reales o imitaciones autorizadas:
Tech @COMMENT_BODY@ Business: Elon Musk (Estilo: Kickboxing experimental, gadgets visuales), Mark Zuckerberg (Estilo: Jiu-Jitsu Brasileño técnico, alta resistencia).
Influencers @COMMENT_BODY@ Content Creators: Logan Paul, Jake Paul, Ibai Llanos, KSI, ElRubius (Estilos adaptados a sus disciplinas reales y atributos físicos exagerados).
Hollywood @COMMENT_BODY@ Cine: Dwayne \"The Rock\" Johnson (Grappler pesado), Jason Statham (Striker rápido), Tom Cruise (Especialista en parkour y takedowns impredecibles).
Música @COMMENT_BODY@ Cultura Pop: Snoop Dogg (Counter-striker evasivo), 50 Cent (Brawler de impacto directo), Bad Bunny (Luchador aéreo/showman).Mecánicas Principales de Gameplay
A. Sistema de Striking (De Pie)
Deformación facial en tiempo real: Cadenas de impacto que causan cortes, hinchazón y sangre procesada por simulación de fluidos.
Gestión de Estamina y Daño Lcalizado: El daño acumulado en las piernas reduce la movilidad; los golpes continuos a la cabeza aumentan la probabilidad de Flash KO.
Momentum del Público: Cuanto más arriesgada o espectacular sea la combinación, más sube la barra de \"Hype\", otorgando un ligero aumento en velocidad de reacción y fuerza.
B. Sistema de Grappling y Suelo (Takedowns @COMMENT_BODY@ Submissions)
Mini-juego de Sumisión Dinámico: Basado en zonas de presión analógicas donde el atacante intenta cerrar la llave (Armbar, Rear-Naked Choke) y el defensor busca el espacio de escape.
Transiciones en Ground @COMMENT_BODY@ Pound: Posicionamiento táctico (Guardia completa, Montada, Control lateral) con mecánicas de bloqueo y codos cortos devastadores.
C. Habilidades Especiales \"Siganture Move\"
Sin romper el tono de realismo físico del deporte, cada personaje posee un movimiento insignia representativo de su persona pública cuando la barra de Showmanship se llena al máximo (por ejemplo, celebraciones virales, golpes característicos o provocaciones al rival que bajan la moral del oponente).
4. Modos de Juego
Modo Carrera: \"Del Podcast al Cinturón\"
Crea tu propio personaje desde cero o toma a una celebridad de nivel bajo.
Gestiona entrenamientos, campamentos de pelea, promociones en redes sociales, ruedas de prensa agresivas y contratos patrocinados.
Mantén la disciplina para no pasarte del peso antes de la ceremonia del pesaje.
Modo Megafight (Local y Multijugador Online)
Combates rápidos online estructurados en divisiones de peso ficticias (Peso Influencer, Peso Pesado de Hollywood, etc.).
Salas de eventos en directo donde la comunidad puede apostar moneda del juego sobre los resultados de las peleas.
Promoter Mode (Gestión de Eventos)
Conviértete en el \"Dana White\" del circuito. Organiza carteleras, pacta las provocaciones (trash talk) pre-pelea para maximizar el PPV, paga las bolsas de los luchadores y evita que las peleas estelares se cancelen por lesiones de última hora.
5. Estilo Visual, Audio y Presentación
Comentaristas Ficticios/Reales: Entradas triunfales de octágono con luces estroboscópicas, música personalizada para cada personaje y comentaristas de renombre que analizan la trayectoria real y la \"carrera en el ring\" del personaje.
Física Ragdoll Mejorada: Las caídas por KO respetan la inercia del impacto final, creando momentos memorables y repetibles al instante en cámara lenta desde múltiples ángulos. (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D MMA game, “Celebrity Octagon Clash,” for phones and tablets, based on the user’s Spanish-language concept.

## Requirements
- Combine technical fighting mechanics with satirical, spectacle-driven celebrity events.
- Include the named real-world celebrity roster, signature moves, career, multiplayer megafights, promoter mode, and event presentation described in the request.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.
- Check the game in-browser and save a small JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with Vite and procedural assets/audio; no external game assets are currently used.
- Keep roster data and fighter stats in Spanish and organized by division.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Vite project configuration and installed dependencies.
- Added roster, division, venue, and commentator data.
- Added a procedural Web Audio engine.
- Added a detailed procedural 3D fighter model, animation poses, damage effects, and ragdoll KO behavior.

### Active
- Build the arena, fighting logic, menus/HUD, and touch-friendly controls.
- Finish integrating fighters and implement playable match modes.
- Run the app, check browser errors and mobile layout, and capture/inspect a JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the existing implementation and continue with the Three.js arena and game loop.
2. Build menus, roster selection, HUD, combat, and responsive touch controls.
3. Run and verify the game in desktop and mobile browsers; capture a JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.
- `src/data/roster.js`: Celebrity roster, stats, signatures, divisions, venues, commentators.
- `src/core/audio.js`: Procedural crowd, combat, and UI audio.
- `src/three/fighter.js`: 3D fighter construction, animations, damage visuals, and KO physics.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no browser verification or screenshot has been done.
- The roster and fighter implementation are only part of the requested game; it is not yet playable.

202: const POSE_EASE = (t) => t * t * (3 - 2 * t)
203: 
204: function samplePose(keys, t) {
205:   if (keys.length === 1) return keys[0].p
206:   t = clamp(t, 0, 1)
207:   for (let i = 0; i < keys.length - 1; i++) {
208:     const a = keys[i]
209:     const b = keys[i + 1]
210:     if (t >= a.t && t <= b.t) {
211:       const k = POSE_EASE((t - a.t) / Math.max(0.0001, b.t - a.t))
212:       const out = {}
213:       for (const j of JOINTS) {
214:         const av = a.p[j]
215:         const bv = b.p[j]
216:         out[j] = [lerp(av[0], bv[0], k), lerp(av[1], bv[1], k), lerp(av[2], bv[2], k)]
217:       }
218:       return out
219:     }
220:   }
221:   return keys[keys.length - 1].p
222: }

224: function makeHair(style, color, headGroup, scale) {
225:   const hairMat = mat(color, 0.92)
226:   const g = new THREE.Group()
227:   const cap = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.115 * scale, 20, 14, 0, TAU, 0, Math.PI * 0.56), hairMat)
228:   cap.position.y = 0.012 * scale
229:   cap.scale.set(1.0, 0.95, 1.04)
230:   cap.castShadow = true
231:   if (style === 'bald') return g
232:   if (style === 'buzz') {
233:     cap.scale.set(0.99, 0.62, 1.02)
234:     cap.position.y = 0.025 * scale
235:     g.add(cap)
236:     return g
237:   }
238:   g.add(cap)
239:   if (style === 'quiff') {
240:     const q = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.055 * scale, 12, 8), hairMat)
241:     q.position.set(0, 0.105 * scale, 0.045 * scale)
242:     q.scale.set(1.5, 0.75, 1.1)
243:     q.rotation.x = -0.35
244:     g.add(q)
245:   } else if (style === 'fluffy') {
246:     for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) {
247:       const b = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.045 * scale, 10, 8), hairMat)
248:       const a = (i / 7) * TAU
249:       b.position.set(Math.cos(a) * 0.065 * scale, 0.075 * scale + Math.sin(i * 2.1) * 0.012 * scale, Math.sin(a) * 0.06 * scale + 0.01)
250:       b.scale.set(1.1, 0.85, 1.1)
251:       g.add(b)
252:     }
253:   } else if (style === 'braids') {
254:     for (let i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
255:       const a = -0.9 + (i / 8) * 1.8
256:       const strand = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CapsuleGeometry(0.011 * scale, 0.19 * scale, 3, 6), hairMat)
257:       strand.position.set(Math.sin(a) * 0.09 * scale, -0.075 * scale, -0.055 * scale - Math.cos(a) * 0.035)
258:       strand.rotation.x = 0.22
259:       strand.rotation.z = Math.sin(a) * 0.22
260:       g.add(strand)
261:     }
262:   }
263:   return g
264: }

608:   applyPose(pose) {
609:     for (const j of JOINTS) {

612:       const v = pose[j]
613:       obj.rotation.set(v[0], v[1], v[2])
614:     }

617:   update(dt, elapsed) {
618:     if (this.koState) {
619:       this.updateKo(dt)
620:       return
621:     }
622:     this.animTime += dt
623:     let keys = POSES[this.anim] || POSES.idle
624:     let t = 1
625:     if (this.anim === 'idle' || this.anim === 'walk' || this.anim === 'groundTop' || this.anim === 'groundBottom') {
626:       const dur = this.anim === 'walk' ? Math.max(0.55, 0.95 - this.moveSpeed * 0.25) : 2.4
627:       t = (this.animTime % dur) / dur
628:     } else {
629:       const attack = ATTACKS[this.anim]
630:       const dur = attack ? attack.dur : 0.5
631:       t = clamp(this.animTime / dur, 0, 1)
632:     }
633:     let target = samplePose(keys, t)
634: 
635:     // flinch overlay
636:     if (this.flinch) {
637:       this.flinchTime += dt
638:       const ft = clamp(this.flinchTime / 0.38, 0, 1)
639:       if (ft >= 1) {
640:         this.flinch = null
641:       } else {
642:         const fpose = samplePose(POSES[this.flinch], ft < 0.5 ? ft * 2 : (1 - ft) * 2)
643:         const w = 0.85 * (1 - Math.abs(ft - 0.35) * 0.6)
644:         for (const j of JOINTS) {
645:           target[j] = [
646:             lerp(target[j][0], fpose[j][0], w),
647:             lerp(target[j][1], fpose[j][1], w),
648:             lerp(target[j][2], fpose[j][2], w),
649:           ]
650:         }
651:       }
652:     }
653: 
654:     // walking bob + breathing
655:     if (this.anim === 'idle' || this.anim === 'walk') {
656:       const bob = Math.sin(elapsed * (this.anim === 'walk' ? 7.5 : 1.9)) * (this.anim === 'walk' ? 0.04 : 0.012)
657:       this.body.position.y = bob
658:       const sway = Math.sin(elapsed * 1.4) * 0.012
659:       target.chest = [target.chest[0] + sway, target.chest[1], target.chest[2]]
660:     } else {
661:       this.body.position.y = lerp(this.body.position.y, 0, Math.min(1, dt * 10))
662:     }
663: 
664:     // smooth towards target
665:     const rate = this.anim.startsWith('hurt') ? 26 : 18
666:     for (const j of JOINTS) {
667:       const c = this.current[j]
668:       const v = target[j]
669:       c[0] = lerp(c[0], v[0], Math.min(1, dt * rate))
670:       c[1] = lerp(c[1], v[1], Math.min(1, dt * rate))
671:       c[2] = lerp(c[2], v[2], Math.min(1, dt * rate))

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D MMA game, “Celebrity Octagon Clash,” for phones and tablets, based on the user’s Spanish-language concept.
- Verify it in-browser and save a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Combine technical fighting mechanics with satirical, spectacle-driven celebrity events.
- Include the named real-world celebrity roster, signature moves, career, multiplayer megafights, promoter mode, and event presentation described in the request.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.
- Check browser errors and mobile layout; capture and inspect a JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js with Vite and procedural assets/audio; no external game assets are currently used.
- Keep roster data and fighter stats in Spanish and organized by division.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Vite project configuration and installed dependencies.
- Added roster, division, venue, and commentator data.
- Added a procedural Web Audio engine.
- Added a detailed procedural 3D fighter model, animation poses, damage effects, and ragdoll KO behavior.
- Inspected the existing project files and confirmed the implementation is not yet a complete playable game.

### Active
- Build the arena, fighting logic, menus/HUD, and touch-friendly controls.
- Finish integrating fighters and implement playable match modes.
- Run and verify the game in desktop and mobile browsers; capture/inspect a JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the Three.js arena and game loop using the existing fighter and roster modules.
2. Build menus, roster selection, HUD, combat, and responsive touch controls.
3. Run and verify the app in desktop and mobile browsers; capture and inspect a JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.
- `src/data/roster.js`: Celebrity roster, stats, signatures, divisions, venues, commentators.
- `src/core/audio.js`: Procedural crowd, combat, and UI audio.
- `src/three/fighter.js`: 3D fighter construction, animations, damage visuals, and KO physics.
- `capture.sh`: Existing browser screenshot capture helper.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no browser verification or screenshot has been done.
- The roster and fighter implementation are only part of the requested game; it is not yet playable.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D mobile/tablet MMA game, “Celebrity Octagon Clash,” from the user’s Spanish-language concept.
- Verify desktop and mobile play in-browser, inspect browser errors/layout, and capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Combine technical fighting mechanics with satirical, spectacle-driven celebrity events.
- Include the requested real-world celebrity roster, signature moves, career, multiplayer megafights, promoter mode, and event presentation.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.
- Provide responsive, usable touch controls.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, Vite, procedural visuals/audio, and Spanish roster data.
- No external game assets are currently used.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Vite configuration/dependencies and roster, division, venue, commentator, audio, and procedural fighter modules.
- Created `index.html` with home, fighter selection, combat HUD/touch controls, pause, and result screens.
- Created `src/style.css` with desktop/mobile layouts and responsive controls.
- Began `src/main.js`: Three.js renderer, procedural arena/cage/crowd/lighting, resize handling, and fighter setup.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js`: selection/menu interactions, match state/combat/AI, controls, HUD, audio, pause, and result handling.
- Build and verify the complete playable game in desktop and mobile browsers; check errors and capture/inspect a JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing gameplay and UI interaction in `src/main.js`.

- Combine technical fighting mechanics with satirical, spectacle-driven celebrity events.
- Include the requested real-world celebrity roster, signature moves, career, multiplayer megafights, promoter mode, and event presentation.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.
- Provide responsive, usable touch controls.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, Vite, procedural visuals/audio, and Spanish roster data.
- No external game assets are currently used.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game markup and responsive styling in `index.html` and `src/style.css`.
- Set up procedural Three.js arena, lighting, crowd, and fighter initialization in `src/main.js`.
- Added division/roster selection rendering, fighter details, mode selection, venue options, and venue palette updates in `src/main.js`.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` interactions and gameplay: match start, combat/AI, keyboard and touch input, HUD, audio, pause, timer, and results.
- Build and verify the game in desktop and mobile browsers; inspect errors/layout and capture/inspect a JPEG screenshot.

- (none)

1. Continue implementing combat loop, player and AI actions, match flow, and remaining UI interactions in `src/main.js`.
2. Run `npm run build` and fix any errors.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens, roster selection, HUD, touch controls, pause and result markup.
- `src/main.js`: Three.js arena and in-progress game/UI logic.
- `src/style.css`: Desktop and mobile game styling.
- `src/data/roster.js`: Roster, stats, signatures, venues, divisions, and helpers.
- `src/three/fighter.js`: Procedural fighters, animation, damage, and KO behavior.
- `src/core/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.
- `capture.sh`: Existing browser screenshot helper.

- Changes are uncommitted.

- Fighter methods include `setAnim`, `hurt`, `setDamage`, `startKo`, `resetKo`, and `dispose`; `ATTACKS` defines available attack parameters.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D mobile/tablet MMA game, “Celebrity Octagon Clash,” from the user’s Spanish-language concept.
- Verify desktop and mobile gameplay in-browser, inspect errors/layout, and capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Combine technical fighting mechanics with satirical, spectacle-driven celebrity events.
- Include the requested real-world celebrity roster, signature moves, career, multiplayer megafights, promoter mode, and event presentation.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them on completion.
- Provide responsive, usable touch controls.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, Vite, procedural visuals/audio, and Spanish roster data.
- No external game assets are currently used.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game markup and responsive styling in `index.html` and `src/style.css`.
- Set up procedural Three.js arena, lighting, crowd, and fighter initialization.
- Added roster/division selection, fighter details, mode selection, venue options, and venue palette updates.
- Added match flow, player movement and attacks, AI combat, keyboard and touch controls, HUD, timer, pause, audio, and results in `src/main.js`.

### Active
- Fix build errors and verify desktop/mobile gameplay, console, responsive layout, and screenshot.

### Blocked
- `npm run build` fails in `src/style.css` with `[postcss] ...:2:755: Unclosed bracket`; fix this before browser verification.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and repair the malformed CSS in `src/style.css`, then rerun `npm run build`.
2. Run the app and test match flow and controls on desktop and mobile; fix any issues.
3. Capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Arena, selection UI, combat loop, AI, controls, match flow.
- `src/style.css`: Styling; current build blocker is an unclosed bracket.
- `index.html`: Game screens, HUD, touch controls, pause and results markup.
- `src/data/roster.js`: Roster, stats, signatures, venues, divisions.
- `src/three/fighter.js`: Procedural fighters, animation, damage, and KO behavior.
- `src/core/audio.js`: Procedural audio engine.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.
- `capture.sh`: Existing browser screenshot helper.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Latest `npm run build` failed during CSS parsing; browser verification and screenshot capture remain undone.
- `Fighter` exposes `def`, `setAnim`, `hurt`, `setDamage`, `startKo`, `resetKo`, `update`, and `dispose`; `ATTACKS` defines move parameters.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and verify “Celebrity Octagon Clash,” a playable, responsive 3D MMA game for desktop and mobile/tablet.

## Requirements
- Combine technical arcade fighting mechanics with satirical, spectacle-driven celebrity events.
- Include the requested celebrity roster, signature moves, career, multiplayer megafights, promoter mode, and event presentation.
- Provide usable keyboard and touch controls; make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, Vite, procedural visuals/audio, and Spanish-language roster data; no external game assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game screens, responsive styling, arena, roster and venue selection, combat loop, AI, controls, HUD, audio, pause, and results.
- Fixed the malformed CSS gradient in `src/style.css`; `npm run build` now succeeds.

### Active
- Fix runtime initialization and then verify desktop/mobile gameplay, console, layout, and screenshots.

### Blocked
- Browser startup throws `TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'hips')` at `Fighter.buildModel` (`src/three/fighter.js:356`); `this.j` is used but not initialized.

## Next Move
1. Initialize the fighter joint map (`this.j`) in `src/three/fighter.js`, then rerun the build.
2. Repeat browser verification; exercise match start, combat, pause, rematch, and mobile touch controls.
3. Capture and inspect desktop/mobile screenshots, including the requested small JPEG if feasible.

## Relevant Files
- `src/three/fighter.js`: Fighter model and animation; current runtime initialization failure.
- `src/main.js`: Game setup, combat, AI, controls, and match flow.
- `src/style.css`: Responsive styling; CSS parse error is fixed.
- `index.html`: Game screens and controls.
- `src/data/roster.js`: Roster, divisions, venues, and fighter stats.
- `src/core/audio.js`: Procedural audio.
- `capture.sh`: Browser screenshot helper; requires `CAPTURE_URL` and `CAPTURE_DIR`.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `npm run build` succeeds with a warning that the minified JS chunk is over 500 kB.
- Capture attempted with `CAPTURE_STRICT=1`; it failed because of the fighter runtime error. A non-strict capture may be used for diagnostics, but no screenshots were produced.
